input.candidate: oh great, another "human rights" expert spewing the same tired talking points. So let me get this straight: you think a fetus is just a "blob of cells" or whatever the latest science-denying phrase is, but a woman's right to, like, actually live her life is somehow compromised by being pregnant? Give me a break. You're not even arguing in good faith, you're just parroting whatever your college feminism class told you to say. Newsflash: most people who think like you actually believe fetuses are human beings, not just "embryos" or whatever. Your condescension is exhausting.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. So, here's the thing: I'm not here to discuss "reproductive rights" or "women's health" or whatever buzzword we're using today. I'm here to say that abortion is a fundamental human right, plain and simple. Don't @ me.

You're probably going to try to spin this as a "pro-life" issue, but let's be real – the only people who care about embryos are the ones who want to control women's lives. Newsflash: we're not going to be lectured by the same people who don't even pay attention to our tax dollars funding actual healthcare.

My position is clear: no government has the right to dictate what a woman can or can't do with her body. Period. Now, are you here to actually engage in a conversation, or just to virtue-signal and pretend to care about "both sides"?

It also asserts that the opponent's belief in the humanity of the fetus is illegitimate without argument.
